summary: Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of Leeds from circa 1984 to 2012 and at Lancaster University around 2012.

Kim Plofker (born 1964) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Haverford College and earned her PhD at Brown University under David Pingree (1995), later holding posts at MIT, Utrecht, and Union College (Assistant Professor 2012, Associate Professor 2019).

Kimberley C. Patton (born 1958) is a religious studies scholar. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1981–1992), where she served as Assistant Professor (~1990–1998) and Professor of the Comparative and Historical Study of Religion (~1998).

Kimiaki Tanaka (born 1955) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, and held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, and Keio University.

Kimmo Koskenniemi (born 1945) is a scholar in computational linguistics who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served as Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki (~1989–2012), where he also directed the BAULT research community.
Kin Cheung is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva (1931–2021) was a historian who studied at the University of London (~1958–1961). He served as a Professor at the University of Ceylon from circa 1969 to 1995.

Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).

Kirill Solonin (born 1969) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as Professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and has held a professorship at Renmin University of China since circa 2013.
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indology scholar who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under teachers including Gopinath Bhattacharya, Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and several traditional pandits, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and at Kyoto University (Bungaku Hakushi), where he served as Professor of Philosophy from 1910 to 1928.

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973) and served as professor at Shitennoji University (~1974) and director of the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute.

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Otani University under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki (1897–1945) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920) and later held posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (~1925–1927).

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as associate professor (attested 2002) and as professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Rissho University. He held posts as a lecturer at Rissho University and as a special researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.
